chunks: He said: The discourse regarding the occultation and the objection to it consists of three aspects.

The first: We compel the Imamiyyah to establish that there is an aspect of ugliness (evil) in it, or in the obligation associated with it, so they are compelled to establish that the occultation does not contain an aspect of ugliness, because if an aspect of ugliness is established, the occultation becomes ugly, even if an aspect of goodness is established in it, as we say regarding the ugliness of imposing what is not bearable (that it has an aspect of ugliness), even if it has an aspect of goodness by being a grace for others.
ai.seo_question: What is the first theological objection regarding the occultation of the Imam?
ai.summary: This passage initiates a dialectical defense of the Imam's occultation by addressing the theological concept of *qubh* (intrinsic evil) versus *husn* (intrinsic good). The author argues that opponents force the Imamiyyah to demonstrate that the occultation is not inherently evil, noting that even if it possesses an evil aspect, it may simultaneously possess a beneficial aspect, such as divine grace (*lutf*), thereby justifying its occurrence despite any perceived detriment.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: Objection of opponents of Imamate He says: The discourse about occultation and criticism thereof consists of three stages:

First objection: We prove to the Imamiyah that occultation involves an evil aspect (qubh), or that imposing obligations during occultation has an evil aspect. They will be required to prove that occultation does not involve any evil aspect, because if evil is involved, occultation becomes evil, though it may carry a good aspect, just as we say in imposing a duty that is beyond one’s capacity, involves an evil aspect, though it may involve a good aspect by being a Lutf (grace) for others.
